title: Floors, sills and anchor points: reading a Dyna Z12 before restoration
author: Caramagnols
excerpt: On a Dyna Z12, the structure often matters more than the general look. Reading the floors and earlier repairs tells you whether you are buying a serious project or only old-car scenery.
content:
On a Dyna Z12, structure often matters more than the general look. Correct paint or a touching interior do not compensate for weak floors, hurried anchor-point repairs or sills that are already tired. That is why the underside so often decides the whole project.

The floor speaks before the shiny body

On a light car, the floor is not secondary sheet metal. It contributes to rigidity and conditions the quality of everything else. Local perforation may remain manageable. A structure weakened in several areas or repaired without method changes the entire nature of the job.

The underside deserves more than a quick glance.

Read anchor points and past repairs

Anchor points, panel joints, weld quality and the real thickness of earlier repairs matter as much as the visible spread of corrosion. An old repair patch may stabilise a zone properly or, on the contrary, hide a worse weakness.

The key is to separate honest repair from simple disguise.

What this changes in budget

When structure is affected, cost does not depend only on the area to remake. It also depends on access, dismantling time, panel shaping and the expected final coherence. A car that looks attractive from afar can become a very heavy project once the underside is read correctly.

The right purchase or restoration therefore begins with a clear structural diagnosis.

Diagnosis before enthusiasm

On our own Dyna, this question belongs to the first serious findings. It forces a calm head, documentation, priorities and a refusal to confuse charm of the model with ease of the work. The real quality of the project is often decided here.

This reference belongs with the page Our Panhard Dyna Z12 in the Gulf of Saint-Tropez. In the same theme, you can also read how to recommission a stored Dyna Z12.
